      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'

        - address

content.text:
The build is green. Here's what I implemented.

## Summary

The `POST /api/owners` pipeline now validates the required owner fields up front and rejects a request that is missing or blank in any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, or `telephone`, responding **400** with a JSON body whose `errors` array names each offending field.

Following the OfficeFloor function-injection conventions in `AGENTS.md`:

1. **New validation step** — `ValidateOwnerFields` (`function/owner/`) is now the first step of the pipeline. It binds `@RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto`, checks each of the five fields for null/blank (`value == null || value.trim().isEmpty()`), and throws a checked `OwnerFieldsInvalidException` listing *all* offending fields at once. On success it republishes the body as `Out<OwnerFieldsDto>`.

2. **`BuildOwner` adjusted** — since only one step per pipeline may bind `@RequestBody`, it now reads the validated body via `@Val OwnerFieldsDto` instead of re-binding the body.

3. **Escalation handler** — `OwnerFieldsInvalidException` (checked, carries the field list) + `OwnerFieldsInvalidExceptionHandler`, wired via `escalation/…OwnerFieldsInvalidException.yml`. It reuses the existing `ProblemDetails` builder and sets an `errors` property, so the 400 body carries `$.errors: ["city", …]`.

4. **Pipeline YAML** — `owners.POST.yml` gained the `validate → build → save → respond` chain (validate under the same `transaction` governance).

The validate step runs before the body is mapped to an entity, so a missing/blank field is a 400 rather than a downstream error.

Test results — all green (`Cp01Tests`: missing city → 400 with `errors` containing `"city"`; blank telephone → 400; complete owner → 2xx), full suite `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`.
